questionText: Which cable type is commonly used to connect a desktop PC to an Ethernet switch?
explanation: Copper twisted-pair Ethernet cabling, such as Cat5e or Cat6, is commonly used to connect PCs to Ethernet switches.

questionText: Which connector is commonly used for copper twisted-pair Ethernet connections?
explanation: Copper twisted-pair Ethernet commonly uses an eight-position, eight-contact modular connector, often called RJ-45.

questionText: Which medium transmits network data using pulses of light?
explanation: Fiber-optic cables transmit data as light through a glass or plastic optical medium rather than electrical signals through copper.

questionText: What is a major advantage of fiber-optic cabling over copper Ethernet cabling?
options: It is immune to electromagnetic interference
It always costs less to install
It carries electrical power to endpoints
explanation: Fiber-optic transmission uses light and is not affected by electromagnetic interference in the same way as electrical signals in copper cables.

questionText: Which type of optical fiber is generally preferred for long-distance telecommunications links?
explanation: Single-mode fiber has a small core and supports optical transmission over long distances with low modal dispersion, making it suitable for long-distance links.

questionText: Which statement accurately describes multimode fiber?
options: It carries electrical signals through copper pairs
It supports multiple propagation modes of light
It is restricted to one optical wavelength in every implementation
It never requires an optical transceiver
explanation: Multimode fiber has a larger core than typical single-mode fiber and allows multiple light propagation modes, which can cause modal dispersion over distance.

questionText: A company needs to connect two network buildings over a distance of several kilometers. Which cabling choice is generally most suitable?
explanation: Single-mode fiber, paired with suitable optical transceivers, is appropriate for kilometer-scale network connections. Standard twisted-pair Ethernet channels have much shorter distance limits.

questionText: What is the usual maximum channel length for 1000BASE-T Ethernet over standards-compliant twisted-pair copper cabling?
explanation: 1000BASE-T Ethernet commonly supports a maximum twisted-pair channel length of 100 meters when suitable cable and installation standards are followed.

questionText: Which Ethernet standard specifies Gigabit Ethernet over twisted-pair copper cabling?
explanation: 1000BASE-T is the Gigabit Ethernet physical-layer specification for twisted-pair copper cabling.

questionText: Which Ethernet technology is designed for short-reach 10 Gigabit Ethernet over suitable multimode fiber?
explanation: 10GBASE-SR is a short-reach 10 Gigabit Ethernet optical standard that operates over supported multimode fiber types.

questionText: A network engineer needs a 10 Gigabit Ethernet optical connection over approximately 10 kilometers of single-mode fiber. Which standard is the most suitable?
explanation: 10GBASE-LR is a long-reach 10 Gigabit Ethernet standard intended for single-mode fiber links up to approximately 10 kilometers under supported conditions.

questionText: What does the abbreviation SFP stand for in networking?
explanation: SFP stands for Small Form-factor Pluggable, referring to a family of removable network transceiver modules.

questionText: What is the primary purpose of an SFP or SFP+ transceiver installed in a compatible network device?
options: Provide a removable physical network interface for a supported medium and speed
Assign VLAN IDs to every connected endpoint
explanation: SFP-family modules provide removable physical-layer connectivity. The supported medium, signaling and speed depend on the module and equipment capabilities.

questionText: Which optical connector is commonly associated with duplex fiber links using SFP transceivers?
explanation: LC connectors are commonly used on duplex fiber patch leads connected to many SFP and SFP+ optical transceivers.

questionText: What does full-duplex operation allow on an Ethernet interface?
options: Transmission and reception at the same time
Transmission only when no other device is sending
Reception without any ability to transmit
Automatic conversion from copper to fiber
explanation: Full-duplex Ethernet allows simultaneous transmission and reception on a link, without the shared-medium collisions associated with half-duplex Ethernet.

questionText: Which statement describes half-duplex Ethernet operation?
options: Both endpoints transmit and receive simultaneously without contention
A device cannot transmit and receive simultaneously on the same shared medium
The link must use optical fiber
The connection automatically operates at 10 Gbps
explanation: Half-duplex Ethernet does not allow simultaneous transmission and reception on the same shared medium and historically uses collision-handling mechanisms such as CSMA/CD.

questionText: One end of a 100 Mbps Ethernet link is forced to full duplex while the other end operates at half duplex. What problem can this create?
options: The link will necessarily become a 10 Gbps connection
Duplex mismatch causing frame errors and poor performance
Automatic conversion of the connection to single-mode fiber
The switch will automatically assign a new IPv4 subnet
explanation: A duplex mismatch can produce poor throughput and interface errors because one side permits simultaneous communication while the other side operates in half duplex.

questionText: A switch interface shows many increasing CRC errors. Which issue is a plausible physical-layer cause?
options: A missing static default route on a remote router
explanation: Damaged or poorly terminated copper cabling can corrupt Ethernet frames, resulting in failed frame check sequence or CRC checks. CRC errors can also have other physical causes.

questionText: An Ethernet interface shows increasing late collisions on a half-duplex link. Which condition should the technician investigate?
options: Excessive collision-domain diameter or a duplex mismatch
explanation: Late collisions can result from an oversized collision domain or duplex mismatch. They indicate an Ethernet media-access or physical-layer problem.

questionText: What is the primary purpose of Auto-MDIX on supported copper Ethernet interfaces?
options: Automatically adjust the transmit and receive pair mapping
Assign an IP address without DHCP
Convert optical signals into radio waves
explanation: Auto-MDIX automatically handles transmit and receive pair orientation on supported copper Ethernet interfaces, reducing the need to choose a straight-through or crossover cable manually.

questionText: Which cable was traditionally used to directly connect two similar 10/100 Mbps Ethernet switch ports when Auto-MDIX was unavailable?
explanation: A crossover cable swaps the transmit and receive pairs used by 10/100 Mbps Ethernet. It was traditionally required for some like-device connections before Auto-MDIX became widespread.

questionText: Which cable is traditionally used to connect a PC Ethernet NIC to a switch access port when Auto-MDIX is unavailable?
explanation: A straight-through copper Ethernet cable was traditionally used between unlike 10/100 Mbps Ethernet interfaces, such as a PC NIC and a switch port.

questionText: What is a primary advantage of shielded twisted-pair cabling compared with unshielded twisted pair in an electrically noisy environment?
options: It eliminates the need for correct termination
It can offer improved protection against electromagnetic interference
It converts Ethernet traffic into optical signals
explanation: Properly installed shielded twisted-pair cabling can reduce the impact of external electromagnetic interference in electrically noisy installations.

questionText: A fiber-optic connection remains down after installing two optical transceivers. Which mismatch should be checked first?
options: Whether the devices use different DNS domains
Whether the transceivers and fiber medium are compatible
Whether the switches have identical hostnames
Whether both interfaces share the same management IP address
explanation: Optical modules must be compatible with their ports, fiber type, wavelengths and link requirements. Mismatched optical media or transceiver specifications can prevent link establishment.

questionText: In a typical duplex fiber connection with separate transmit and receive strands, how should the strands be connected?
options: Transmit to transmit and receive to receive
Both strands to the transmit connector
Transmit on one endpoint to receive on the other endpoint
Either strand orientation always works without checking
explanation: For conventional two-fiber duplex links, the transmit side of each endpoint connects to the receive side of the opposite endpoint.

questionText: A copper Ethernet interface is configured with the shutdown command on Cisco IOS. What should the interface status normally indicate?
options: Err-disabled due to a CRC error
explanation: The shutdown command administratively disables the interface. Cisco IOS reports the interface as administratively down until it is enabled with no shutdown.

questionText: Which Cisco IOS command displays detailed Ethernet interface statistics, including errors and packet counters?
explanation: The show interfaces command displays physical and data-link status, traffic counters, errors and other interface information.

questionText: A switch port is up, but a connected application experiences poor throughput and the interface counter shows increasing input errors. What is the best initial troubleshooting action?
options: Inspect the physical cable, connectors and negotiated link settings
Disable all routing protocols on the network
explanation: Input errors can originate from cabling, connectors, interference or speed and duplex issues. Checking the physical path and negotiated interface settings is an appropriate initial step.

questionText: Which statement about Cat6a cabling is correct?
options: It is exclusively an optical fiber standard
It is designed to support 10GBASE-T over a standards-compliant 100-meter channel
It cannot be used for Gigabit Ethernet
explanation: Category 6A cabling is designed to support 10GBASE-T Ethernet over a standards-compliant channel of up to 100 meters and also supports lower Ethernet speeds.

questionText: An optical link has excessive attenuation and intermittently loses connectivity. Which action is most appropriate?
options: Inspect and clean the fiber connectors and check the optical power budget
Change the local PC's default gateway address
Configure a new DNS search domain
explanation: Dirty connectors, damaged fibers and excessive link loss can reduce received optical power. Inspecting and cleaning connectors and verifying the optical power budget are appropriate troubleshooting steps.
